DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Venous Insufficiency with Venous Stasis Ulcer.

Based on the 10-year history of bilateral leg swelling, your family history, prior DVT, and the 6-month duration of the wound on the right lower leg, the clinical picture strongly points to chronic venous insufficiency. The lack of significant improvement despite the wound's presence, combined with the chronic edema, indicates that venous hypertension has compromised the skin integrity in the gaiter area. While the Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) was requested earlier to rule out arterial disease, the timeline and specific risk factors you provided make a primary venous etiology the most likely cause. I recommend continuing with compression therapy and wound care to promote healing, but please follow up with a vascular specialist if the wound does not show improvement within two weeks.
